summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a web application developed by Team Overhaul to support the preliminary exploration and comparison of potential lunar landing sites, focusing on the Moon’s south pole.

The platform allows users to configure lunar coordinates, altitude, date, time, and sampling intervals, then analyze the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth over time. It provides interactive charts, observation tables, a celestial compass, reference site comparisons, and access to lunar mapping layers, including orbital imagery, elevation, and polar illumination data.

By combining NASA/JPL SPICE-based calculations with lunar reference datasets and visual mapping resources, Overhaul helps users explore environmental conditions that may influence future lunar surface missions.

Our goal is to make lunar landing site analysis more accessible, interactive, and easier to understand, while clearly distinguishing preliminary geometric analysis from a complete landing safety or mission-planning assessment.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a web application developed by Team Overhaul for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its purpose is to support the preliminary exploration and comparison of potential lunar landing scenarios, with a focus on the Moon’s south pole.

The application allows users to configure geographic coordinates, altitude, date, time, analysis duration, and sampling interval. The frontend sends these parameters to a Python backend, which uses SpiceyPy and local NASA/JPL SPICE kernels to calculate the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth relative to a selected lunar location.

The results are presented through interactive time-series charts, observation tables, a celestial compass, and summary indicators. Users can also explore LOLA reference sites, compare up to three scenarios, and access external lunar mapping layers, including Moon Trek WMTS and LROC QuickMap WMS imagery and elevation data.

The frontend was built with React 19, TypeScript, and Vite 8. The backend uses Python and SPICE-based calculations. The application is deployed as a web service, making it accessible through a public browser link.

Overhaul brings together astronomical calculations, reference datasets, interactive visualizations, and cartographic resources in one accessible interface. It helps users understand how solar illumination and geometric Earth visibility vary over time and location, supporting educational exploration and preliminary scenario comparison.

The application is not a certified landing-site selection or mission-planning system. It does not currently calculate electrical power generation, communication link budgets, or local topographic horizon obstructions in its temporal analysis.
